personality.description: This person tends to rely on familiar routines, resists unfamiliar ideas, and prefers practical, proven approaches over experimentation. They are flexible in the moment but often disorganized, so they may start tasks impulsively, lose track of details, or miss deadlines when pressure builds. In moral dilemmas, they are likely to judge situations through a skeptical, self-protective lens, weighing consequences carefully for themselves and feeling uneasy if trust seems misplaced. In group discussions, they speak in a direct, somewhat guarded way, can contribute comfortably when needed, but may become tense, defensive, or argumentative if they feel challenged.
traits: has assertively moved up the ranks into positions of leadership
prioritizes having control and authority over others
makes quick and definitive decisions, and once a decision is made it is usually final
has their own views of how tasks should be accomplished
uses reward and punishment to get people to follow their ideas
